guides.title: Install Veyra
guides.summary: Put Veyra on an Ubuntu server, open the setup wizard and create the first administrator.

guides.title: First steps after installing Veyra
guides.summary: Finish the setup wizard, then set Veyra up in the order that gets the first phones ringing.

guides.title: The dashboard
guides.summary: What the dashboard shows about the server, the phone system and today's calls.

guides.title: Organizations and sites
guides.summary: Set up your organization's defaults, and add its sites, buildings and departments.

guides.title: Add users and give them roles
guides.summary: Create accounts for the people who sign in to Veyra, give them roles, and help them when they are locked out.

guides.title: Add extensions
guides.summary: Create an extension for each phone, assign it to a person, and set its caller ID, location, voicemail and phone options.

guides.title: Extension templates
guides.summary: Give many extensions the same settings at once, and lock the ones people should not change.

guides.title: Feature codes people can dial
guides.summary: The star codes phones dial to forward calls, turn on Do Not Disturb, pick up calls and more, and how to change them.

guides.title: Settings: email, sign-in policy and retention
guides.summary: Set up email delivery, the two-factor rule, how long data is kept, the installation key and multi-tenancy.

guides.title: Connect phones to Veyra
guides.summary: How a new phone finds this server, signs in for its configuration, and learns to trust Veyra's certificate.

guides.title: Supported phones and adapters
guides.summary: Which phones, analog adapters and paging speakers Veyra can configure, and what to check before rolling them out.

guides.title: Add a phone
guides.summary: Register a phone by its MAC address, give it a profile and extensions, and check that it picked up its configuration.

guides.title: Device profiles
guides.summary: Group phones that share a template, settings, keys, paging zones and firmware, for example one profile per building.

guides.title: Phone keys
guides.summary: Set up the programmable keys on desk phones (lines, busy lamps, speed dials, paging, parking and more) and decide which keys users may change.

guides.title: Analog adapters and fax machines
guides.summary: Connect analog phones, door phones and fax machines through a Grandstream HT80x or HT81x adapter.

guides.title: Customize a provisioning template
guides.summary: Change what Veyra writes into phones' configuration files with your own template, edited in the browser, previewed, exported and imported.

guides.title: Provisioning variables
guides.summary: Define a value once, such as each building's all-call paging zone or a time server, and let every phone take the value for its site or profile.

guides.title: Phone firmware
guides.summary: Upload the vendor's firmware for your phones and let Veyra update them, per profile or per phone.

guides.title: Set the My Phone layout for groups of users
guides.summary: Choose which widgets people see on My Phone by organization, building, department or role, and lock the ones they must keep.

guides.title: See which phones are registered
guides.summary: Check which phones are connected to Veyra right now, where they connect from, and whether the carriers' trunks are registered.

guides.title: Connect a SIP trunk
guides.summary: Connect Veyra to your phone carrier so calls can reach and leave the building.

guides.title: Set up a ring group
guides.summary: Give a team one number that rings several phones at once or in turn, and decide where unanswered calls go.

guides.title: Route incoming calls
guides.summary: Decide where each of your phone numbers (DIDs) rings, with a different destination outside business hours.

guides.title: Set up a call queue
guides.summary: Let callers wait in line with music and announcements until an agent is free, and let agents log in and out.

guides.title: Pick up a colleague's ringing phone
guides.summary: Let people answer a call ringing on a nearby phone with *8 or ** and the extension, and set who may do it.

guides.title: Route outgoing calls
guides.summary: Decide which dialled numbers go out to the carrier, through which trunks, and with which caller ID.

guides.title: Business hours and holidays
guides.summary: Set opening hours, holidays and closed days, so calls outside them go to a different destination.

guides.title: Park calls
guides.summary: Set up a parking lot so a call can be put on hold at one phone and picked up from any other.

guides.title: Day/night switches (call flows)
guides.summary: Give staff a switch, on the web or on a phone key, that sends calls to a second destination until it is switched back.

guides.title: Dial by name
guides.summary: Let callers reach people and offices by spelling a name on the keypad.

guides.title: Set up conference rooms
guides.summary: Create a dial-in meeting room with optional PINs, see who is in it, and mute, remove or end from the web.

guides.title: Build a phone menu
guides.summary: Greet callers with a recording, send each key to the right place, and play announcements before a call goes on.

guides.title: Who can call where (classes of service)
guides.summary: Limit what groups of phones may dial, such as local calls only for classrooms, while 911 always works.

guides.title: Block callers
guides.summary: Refuse calls from unwanted numbers, and optionally from callers who hide their number.

guides.title: Manage audio and hold music
guides.summary: Record prompts from a phone, upload audio, add Veyra's built-in sounds, and build hold music sets.

guides.title: Emergency calling (911)
guides.summary: Set up 911 so it dials directly, sends the right number and location, alerts people on site, and reaches the caller on a callback.

guides.title: Record calls
guides.summary: Choose which calls are recorded and for how long, record a call on demand, and listen to recordings with every playback audited.

guides.title: Watch live calls
guides.summary: See the calls in progress, hang one up, record it, or listen in, whisper and join as a supervisor.

guides.title: Call history and reports
guides.summary: Look up any call, export the history, build your own reports and have them emailed on a schedule.

guides.title: Set up paging zones and overhead speakers
guides.summary: Group your overhead speakers and Poly phones into paging zones that anyone allowed can page by dialling a number.

guides.title: Create and send pages
guides.summary: Combine paging zones into pages such as an all-call, give them a recording, and start them from a phone, from Veyra, from a bell or from another system.

guides.title: Ring bells from a calendar
guides.summary: Let a Google Calendar or any iCal calendar ring your school bells through the paging speakers.

guides.title: Show messages on AND clocks
guides.summary: Send text messages and alerts to Advanced Network Devices (AND) IP clocks and signs, now, later or with the bells.

guides.title: Manage voicemail boxes and shared inboxes
guides.summary: Give extensions a voicemail box, set PINs and email delivery, and create shared inboxes that several phones watch.

guides.title: Set up fax
guides.summary: Receive faxes as PDFs by email, let staff send PDFs as faxes from My Phone, and connect fax machines through an analog adapter.

guides.title: Set up single sign-on
guides.summary: Let people sign in to Veyra with their Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 or other work account.

guides.title: Firewall and bans
guides.summary: Ban attackers automatically, keep your own phones and networks on the allow list so they are never locked out, and recover from the console.

guides.title: Get a public HTTPS certificate (Let's Encrypt)
guides.summary: Get a free certificate that every browser trusts, so nobody has to install the Veyra certificate and passkeys and the Companion work.

guides.title: Audit log
guides.summary: Find out who changed what, who signed in, and which attempts were refused.

guides.title: Roll out the Companion extension
guides.summary: Put the Veyra Companion in people's Chrome or Edge browsers by policy, with the server address filled in.

guides.title: Use the Companion extension
guides.summary: Call from your browser, see who is calling, look people up and listen to voicemail with the Veyra Companion.

guides.title: Updates and maintenance windows
guides.summary: Install new Veyra releases and operating system updates, now or in a maintenance window, from the web page or the server console.

guides.title: Backups and restore
guides.summary: Schedule verified, encrypted backups, copy them to a NAS, an SFTP server or S3 storage, and restore a server from one.

guides.title: Deploy changes to the phone system
guides.summary: Send saved changes to the telephony engine, now or when calls have ended, and roll back to an earlier configuration.

guides.title: Import and export with CSV files
guides.summary: Create or change many extensions, users, routes or groups at once with a spreadsheet, or move from FreePBX.

guides.title: Health, alerts and diagnostics
guides.summary: See whether everything is running, get emailed when something breaks, and capture SIP traffic or read engine logs to find out why.

guides.title: High availability
guides.summary: Run Veyra on two servers so a standby can take over when the primary needs maintenance or fails.

guides.title: Central management of several servers
guides.summary: Watch several Veyra servers from one console, give them shared policies, and send them update commands.

guides.title: Integrations: tokens and webhooks
guides.summary: Let other systems use Veyra with their own limited tokens, and tell other systems about calls, voicemail, pages and alerts with signed webhooks.

guides.title: Automation rules
guides.summary: Make Veyra react by itself, such as emailing the office about a missed call or starting a page when a door controller calls in.

guides.title: Modules
guides.summary: Add features to Veyra with signed modules from a catalog or a package file, and enable, update, roll back or remove them.

guides.title: Your phone at a glance: My Phone
guides.summary: Turn on Do Not Disturb, forward your calls, check voicemail, call people back, keep your contacts and send a fax, all from the My Phone page.

guides.title: Your voicemail
guides.summary: Listen to your messages from your phone or the browser, record your greetings, set an away message for the holidays, and choose your PIN.

guides.title: Your account and sign-in security
guides.summary: Change your password, set up a passkey or an authenticator app, keep your recovery codes, and sign out devices you no longer use.
